experience: My assistant prints the PDF report and the one-paragraph answer goes at the top of my board pack. That is the only part I read properly.
The side-panel chat is where P2 deals with them. I never see it and I don't want to. P2 says she gets answers there without waiting for a meeting, which I take as a good sign.

On day 10 I tell P2 in our Monday meeting that the board wants the satellite clinic covered too. She types it into the side panel and it 'turns into page changes'. Nothing tells me the scope, price or deadline changed. I only hear if P2 tells me.
Before signing I'd read the security one-pager and the sample report, both PDFs. That's fine.
Worry: answers in a chat that change the scope or the findings. Someone at the consultancy has to approve that, and I want it on paper with my name or P2's on it.
what_reaches_you: Pre-sale PDF pack: price, turnaround, sample report, security one-pager
Whatever P2 forwards or tells me in meetings
Nothing directly: notifications go to whoever acts, which is P2
Z.quote: P2 tells me it's easy to change course in their chat. Fine. But when the board widens the question, I want a one-page letter saying what changed, what it costs and when I get it. I don't want a sentence buried in a chat log.

experience: This is the one that looks most like a consultancy to me: a formal document at the end, plus a dashboard P2 can screenshot for me ('data 80% complete, analysis 60%').
Those percentages are dangerous. They're exactly what I'd put in front of the board, and 'analysis 60%' means nothing. The board will ask me 'so when?' and I won't have an answer.

The satellite clinic doesn't fit a 5-step form that was finished on day 1. P2 would have to go back and redo the form, or email the consultant. I suspect it becomes a new engagement and a new invoice.
My assistant could at least print the dashboard. That's more than I get from the others.
what_reaches_you: Probably a change-order email if scope widens, which is what I actually want
Y.quote: It looks like something I'd pay for. But a form P2 filled in on day one won't absorb the board changing its mind on day ten, and I'm not paying twice for one question.

experience: I'd never see it. The whole engagement lives in a chat thread between P2 and the consultant.

For a hospital spending real money with a board watching, 'it's all in a chat' sounds informal to me. The report still comes out as a PDF, so the end product is fine. The process just isn't anything I could show anyone.
Reframing is easiest here. P2 types 'the board also wants a satellite clinic assessment'. But I have no idea if that's in scope, priced or approved. It's a conversation. It isn't a contract change.
If P2 goes on leave, nobody can tell where things stand without scrolling through a thread.
W.quote: You're asking me to sign off a hospital engagement that's run like a WhatsApp group. The report may be excellent, but I can't show the board the path to it.

experience: The 'Your next step' card with an owner and a time is what P2 can read out to me in a meeting: 'waiting on our DPO, expected Thursday'. That's the status I want: who is holding it up and when it moves.
The progress tracker in words (Understand to Report) is something my assistant could paste into an email to me. It's honest, unlike percentages.

Editable 'What we understood' lines. P2 changes the goal to add the satellite clinic, and it's written down as the agreed problem statement. That's closer to a record. I'd still want it to trigger a formal confirmation to me.
No chat. If P2 has a quick question she waits for the consultant. That's her problem, not mine, but it slows things down.
what_reaches_you: P2's verbal or forwarded status: next step, owner, date, stage
Final report PDF/Word in board-ready form
X.quote: Tell me what stage we're at, who's holding it up and when it lands. If P2 can say that in one sentence on Monday, I'm happy.

feature_to_sign: An executive email or PDF, sent to me or my assistant without any login, that goes out every week and whenever scope changes. It should give: the question we're answering, stage, who is holding things up, expected report date, cost impact, and a one-click 'approve scope change' reply. When the board adds the satellite clinic, I want to confirm the new scope, price and date on that one page by email, not have it slip in through P2's chat.
